title: Exact localization of fixed tensor and its normalized resolving comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], homotopy category $K(R)$ and unbounded derived localization $Q_h:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the triangulated structure of $K(R)$ and the exact functor $Q_h$ of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Use the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the resolving full subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of flat-term K-flat complexes, and the published bifunctor $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ with its specified natural comparison $c_{P,S}:Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R S)\cong T(Q_hP,Q_hS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Fix a K-flat complex $A$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Assume the fixed tensor operations $H_A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ and $H^A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R A)$ induce additive exact functors on $K(R)$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], invert quasi-isomorphisms after applying $Q_h$, and use the coherent signed shift maps $s^2_n,s^1_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts].
There exist additive exact functors $G_A,G^A:D(R)\to D(R)$ and natural isomorphisms $\eta_L:Q_hH_A\cong G_AQ_h$ and $\eta_R:Q_hH^A\cong G^AQ_h$. Their coherent integer-shift comparisons are the unique ones for which $\eta_L,\eta_R$ commute with shifts and restrict to $Q_hs^2_n,Q_hs^1_n$, with the canonical shift comparisons of $Q_h$ inserted. The functors carry every distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle with its connecting arrow.
There are unique natural isomorphisms $d_L:G_A\cong T(Q_hA,-)$ and $d_R:G^A\cong T(-,Q_hA)$ for which $(d_L)_{Q_hP}(\eta_L)_P=c_{A,P}$ and $(d_R)_{Q_hP}(\eta_R)_P=c_{P,A}$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_R$. If $r:P\to B$ is any quasi-isomorphism with $P\in\mathcal P_R$, the composite comparisons $e_L=(d_LQ_h)\eta_L$ and $e_R=(d_RQ_h)\eta_R$ have components
$$e_{L,B}=T(1,Q_hr)c_{A,P}(Q_hH_A(r))^{-1},\qquad e_{R,B}=T(Q_hr,1)c_{P,A}(Q_hH^A(r))^{-1}.$$
These formulas are independent of $r$ and are natural for every derived varying-argument map through $d_L,d_R$. The factorization with its signed shifts and normalized comparisons is unique up to its unique compatible natural isomorphism. No boundedness or flatness of cohomology is required.

proof.text: Put $Q=Q_h$. Treat either side simultaneously: take $(H,G,\eta)=(H_A,G_A,\eta_L)$ or $(H^A,G^A,\eta_R)$, and put $U=QH$. The hypotheses say exactly that $U$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The homotopy localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] give $G:D(R)\to D(R)$ and an isomorphism $\eta:U\cong GQ$ (the inverse of the comparison in that clause). This construction does not require choosing resolutions. The exactness of $Q$ is supplied by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated].

source.place: Tags 04VG/04VK (lemma-properties-left-localization, lemma-properties-right-localization); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU, paragraph preceding definition-derived-tor

proof.text: Both $K(R)$ and $D(R)$ are additive, and $Q$ is additive because it is exact [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Thus $U=QH$ is additive by the assumed additivity of $H$. Every derived object is isomorphic to $QB$ for a complex $B$, by the localization construction in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-pur-additive-localization-descent] with $q=Q$, target $D(R)$, and comparison $\eta^{-1}:GQ\cong U$. All its hypotheses now hold, so $G$ is additive. This applies separately to $G_A$ and $G^A$.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization); additive descent via the cited additive-localization theorem

proof.text:
Write $q_n(B):Q(B[n])\cong(QB)[n]$ for the canonical comparisons of $Q$, and $h_n(B):H(B[n])\cong HB[n]$ for $s^2_n$ on the left or $s^1_n$ on the right [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts, lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Set $u_n(B)=q_n(HB)\circ Q(h_n(B))$. On precomposition with $Q$, define a natural isomorphism from $G(-[n])$ to $(G-)[n]$ by components
$$a_n(B)=\eta_B[n]\circ u_n(B)\circ\eta_{B[n]}^{-1}\circ G(q_n(B)^{-1}).$$
Every factor is natural in $B$, so this really is a transformation on the precomposed functors. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], applied to these two functors on $D(R)$ and their identity factorization comparisons, extends $a_n$ uniquely to $\sigma_n:G(-[n])\cong(G-)[n]$. Extend the displayed componentwise inverse too; preservation of composition and uniqueness show that the extensions are inverse. By construction,
$$\sigma_n(QB)\circ G(q_n(B))\circ\eta_{B[n]}=\eta_B[n]\circ q_n(HB)\circ Q(h_n(B)).$$
This is the required signed normalization and shift compatibility of $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), transformation full faithfulness; explicit conjugation, as in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Shift/Localization.lean commShiftOfLocalization

proof.text: The comparisons $u_n$ obey the zero and addition laws: they are the comparisons of the composite $QH$, obtained by first applying $Q$ to $h_n$ and then $q_n$; the two laws follow by substituting the laws of $h_n$ and $q_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts, lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Check the laws for $\sigma_n$ after precomposition with $Q$. In the zero law the adjacent $\eta_B^{-1}\eta_B$ cancel and $u_0$ is the canonical zero comparison. In the addition law, substitute the equation of Step 3 for the successive shifts $n$ and $m$. Naturality of $\eta$ moves the intermediate shift-identification map across $\eta$; the intermediate $\eta_{B[n]}^{-1}\eta_{B[n]}$ cancels. The result is the addition law for $u_{n+m}$, with the canonical $q$ identifications. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives equality on all derived objects. The same clause shows uniqueness of every $\sigma_n$, since compatibility with $\eta$ forces precisely $a_n$ on precomposition. Thus these are coherent integer shifts.

source.place: Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), faithfulness on transformations; zero/addition identities by conjugation

proof.text:
Let $\Delta$ be a distinguished derived triangle. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], it is isomorphic to $Q\Delta_0$ for a cone triangle $\Delta_0=(X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ of $K(R)$. The hypothesis on $H$ says $H\Delta_0$ is distinguished with last arrow $h_1(X)\circ H(w)$, so its image under the exact $Q$ is distinguished [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. The first two naturality squares of $\eta$ compare this triangle to $G(Q\Delta_0)$. For the last square, naturality at $w$ and Step 3 give explicitly
$$\sigma_1(QX)\circ G(q_1(X))\circ G(Qw)\circ\eta_Z
=\eta_X[1]\circ q_1(HX)\circ Q(h_1(X))\circ Q(Hw).$$
Hence the three components $\eta_X,\eta_Y,\eta_Z$ give an isomorphism of triangles, including the connecting arrow. Distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism [def-weil-triangulated-category], so $G(Q\Delta_0)$, and then $G\Delta$, are distinguished. Together with Step 2 this proves exactness of both functors for the specified shifts.

proof.text:
Let $L=Q|_{\mathcal P_R}$. The induced equivalence $J:W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\to D(R)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies $L$ with the fraction localization followed by $J$. Therefore $L$ is a localization: for any target, precomposition with $J$ is an equivalence (inverse given by precomposition with an inverse equivalence), and then precomposition with the fraction localization has the universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. In particular restriction along $L$ is fully faithful on transformations between functors on $D(R)$. Since $A\in\mathcal P_R$, the specified $c_{A,P}$ are natural in $P\in\mathcal P_R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Thus
$$b_P=c_{A,P}\circ(\eta_L)_P^{-1}:G_A(LP)\cong T(QA,LP)$$
is a natural isomorphism on the restrictions. Extend it and its inverse along $L$ by clause (2) of the universal property. Their composites extend the identities and hence are identities. This gives a unique natural isomorphism $d_L:G_A\cong T(QA,-)$ with the claimed normalization.

For the right-hand operation the same restriction calculation starts with the natural isomorphism
$$b'_P=c_{P,A}\circ(\eta_R)_P^{-1}:G^A(LP)\cong T(LP,QA).$$
Its naturality is the first-variable naturality explicitly included in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The fully faithful restriction along $L$ established in Step 6, using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], extends $b'$ and its inverse to inverse transformations. It yields the unique $d_R:G^A\cong T(-,QA)$ with $(d_R)_{QP}(\eta_R)_P=c_{P,A}$. No shift structure on the published bifunctor is assumed or used for this identification.

proof.text:
Put $e_L=(d_LQ)\eta_L$ and $e_R=(d_RQ)\eta_R$. For any quasi-isomorphism $r:P\to B$ with $P\in\mathcal P_R$, naturality gives
$$e_{L,B}\circ QH_A(r)=T(1,Qr)\circ c_{A,P},\qquad e_{R,B}\circ QH^A(r)=T(Qr,1)\circ c_{P,A}.$$
The maps $QH_A(r)$ and $QH^A(r)$ are invertible by the explicit hypothesis; compose on the right with their inverses to obtain exactly the two formulas in the statement. Such an $r$ exists for every unbounded $B$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Each formula equals the already defined $e$ component, so two different resolutions give equal answers without selecting a comparison between their resolutions. Naturality for an arbitrary map $v:M\to N$ of $D(R)$ is the identity
$$d_{L,N}\circ G_A(v)=T(1,v)\circ d_{L,M},$$
and its right-hand counterpart; these hold because $d_L,d_R$ are natural transformations on $D(R)$, not merely on representatives. In particular they apply to inverse quasi-isomorphisms and to their composites. The representative values used above are the specified comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); naturality and inversion of the displayed equations

proof.text: Finally suppose $(\widetilde G,\widetilde\eta)$ is another factorization of either $U$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives exactly one isomorphism $\theta:G\cong\widetilde G$ with $(\theta Q)\eta=\widetilde\eta$. It respects the shifts: after precomposition with $Q$ the required square reduces, by this equality and the normalization equation of Step 3, to the identical $u_n$ comparison on each side; clause (3) gives the square on $D(R)$. Its compatibility with the normalized $d$ follows after restriction along $L$: both composites with $\eta_P$ are $c_{A,P}$ on the left, or $c_{P,A}$ on the right. Faithfulness along $L$ from Step 6 proves the equality globally. This proves the final uniqueness assertion, with its signed shifts and normalized comparisons. The only resolutions used are those of [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], whose statement has no boundedness or cohomological-flatness hypothesis.

No SGA is used. Each step checked against the cited statements: Step 1, clause (1) gives G and eta = phi^-1. Step 2, every hypothesis of additive-localization-descent holds (Q additive because exact, H additive by hypothesis, essential surjectivity, e = eta^-1). Step 3, I type-checked a_n: G((QB)[n]) -> GQ(B[n]) -> QH(B[n]) -> (QHB)[n] -> (GQB)[n], extended by clause (2) with identity comparisons. Step 4, the zero and addition laws hold by conjugation and clause (3). Step 5, I re-derived the connecting square from the Step 3 normalization and the naturality of eta at w, then TR1. Steps 6-7, L = J composed with the fraction localization is a localization; b_P = c_{A,P} eta_P^-1 is natural on P_R and extends uniquely. Step 8, naturality of e at a resolution r gives the formulas, QH(r) is invertible by hypothesis, and independence of r is equality to e_B. Step 9, theta comes from clause (2) with tau = id, and the shift and d compatibilities follow by faithfulness. Edge cases: n=0, the sign (-1)^{np} on the left side only, zero complexes, r=id gives c, unbounded complexes. Duplicate search over the whole DAG found nothing that states the item or replaces Steps 3-5: the exact-functor-derived nodes are termwise-abelian only, and left-derived-exact-chosen-localization has no eta-normalization.
